equation_summary: Plain causal softmax attention w = softmax((q·kᵀ)·(1/sqrt(d))·mask − 1e9·(1−mask)) · v (attention_impl, fp32 upcast for fp16) with four exact static sparsity patterns: 'all' = causal band (matrix_band_part lower triangle); 'local' = causal band of bandwidth local_attn_ctx; 'strided' = keys j with j ≤ i and (i−j) mod stride == 0 (implemented blockwise on a strided-transposed layout); 'fixed' = per-head block layout where each query block attends to its local block row plus specific strided columns (layout[q, idx::stride]) with causal cut-off, heads cycling through num_verts sub-patterns. The blocksparse path uses a block-level layout plus a positionwise mask callback (diagonal blocks lower-triangular; local blocks banded).
ledger_verdicts: CONFIRM `E[QKV/source all/local/strided/fixed pattern] ; U1.S[exact blocks] ; E[output]`: attention.py:8-29 (get_attn_mask) defines exact all/local/strided masks and attention.py:114-182 (get_blocksparse_obj) defines the fixed per-head block layouts; the mixer itself is stock softmax (attention.py:76-86, 100-104).

CONFIRM 'B[indexed_K1_schedule]; compare optimized source traversal, not dense masked SDPA': the source's optimized path is the blocksparse kernels over an explicit block layout (attention.py:90-111), so efficient URM coverage needs the indexed-K1 schedule; the dense attention_impl is only the correctness oracle.

NOTE: 'strided' is realized by a data-layout transpose (strided_transpose, attention.py:32-39) feeding block-diagonal block chunks — the logical source pattern is the (q−k) mod stride == 0 set; the transpose is a physical-schedule detail that the descriptor must not bake into semantics.
NOTE: masking uses finite -1e9 rather than -inf (attention.py:82) — a numerical-policy difference from U1.S defaults that parity tests must match.
axis: A2 locality routing / indexed K1 schedule (B[indexed_K1_schedule])
